issue_snapshot.title: CPU unrolled pressure oracle silently returns nonfinite gradients beyond the float32 roundoff floor
issue_snapshot.first_found: S-19 CPU rehearsal; historical v0.3.0 and R-0058 records already contain the output
issue_snapshot.notes: Present since v0.3.0: unrolled_channel_pressure_solve_oracle is a CPU-only test reference exported through the deprecated functional facade. Beyond the float32 roundoff floor its forward solve restores a valid state, but backward silently produces nonfinite gradients. Claude confirmed finite gradients at 5/10/20 iterations, versus 167/192 and 2815/3072 nonfinite elements at 50/200 iterations for fixed_float32_roundoff_floor and fixed_float32_floor_crossing. Production, transpose and implicit remain finite. D-0022 permits only these exact oracle/gradient records in S-19; their entire raw tensor bytes must match across baseline A/B and candidate, otherwise N/FAIL. Every other nonfinite result remains H/STOP. No runtime change or closure in S-19. Before S-20 freeze the user decides a separate reviewed fix or acceptance as a documented limitation. Older-version effects have not been established.
